sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `opencode`
- Canonical name: OpenCode under Anomaly (`claim-opencode-w2-identity`)
- Current status: active v1.18.16 release at capture (`claim-opencode-w2-status`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-10

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: an MIT-licensed local agent runtime with terminal, desktop, web, IDE, API, and CI clients (`claim-opencode-w2-primary-type`, `claim-opencode-w2-license`, `claim-opencode-w2-unique`).
- What it is not: a runtime with an agent-enforced security sandbox (`claim-opencode-w2-not-for`). A public share page is a transcript viewer, not an agent-control surface (`claim-opencode-w2-surface-share`).

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` (`claim-opencode-w2-primary-type`)
- Agent-loop owner: the OpenCode core session runner owns context, provider turns, tool execution, persistence, and continuation (`claim-opencode-w2-loop-owner`).
- Architecture: local runtime by default, with direct remote clients and a configured GitHub Actions runner documented as separate surfaces (`claim-opencode-w2-execution`, `claim-opencode-w2-surface-attach`, `claim-opencode-w2-surface-desktop`, `claim-opencode-w2-surface-ci`).

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-opencode-cli-tui`, `surface-opencode-cli-run`, `surface-opencode-web-local`, `surface-opencode-web-lan`, `surface-opencode-attach-tui`, `surface-opencode-desktop-local`, `surface-opencode-desktop-wsl`, `surface-opencode-desktop-remote-http`, `surface-opencode-ide`, `surface-opencode-acp`, `surface-opencode-local-api`, `surface-opencode-github-actions`, `surface-opencode-share-page`.
- Execution location: same-device local runtime, direct user-controlled remote backend, or configured GitHub Actions runner (`claim-opencode-w2-execution`, `claim-opencode-w2-surface-attach`, `claim-opencode-w2-surface-desktop`, `claim-opencode-w2-surface-ci`).

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: broad provider and model selection, including local models; stable product-wide fallback is unknown (`claim-opencode-w2-provider-auth`).
- Auth strategy: provider-specific API keys, OAuth, and subscription reuse for named providers (`claim-opencode-w2-provider-auth`).
- Provider support: official docs claim 75+ providers plus local models (`claim-opencode-w2-provider-auth`).

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: project AGENTS.md initialization and project/global configuration, multi-scope skill discovery, and snapshots are documented in separate ledger claims (`claim-opencode-w2-context-behavior`, `claim-opencode-w2-skills`, `claim-opencode-w2-snapshots`).
- Memory: a separate persistent-memory feature remains unknown.
- Compaction: automatic compaction with optional pruning and a 10,000-token reserve is documented (`claim-opencode-w2-compaction`).
- Session behavior: server controls and CLI continue/import/export controls are separate (`claim-opencode-w2-context-session`, `claim-opencode-w2-session-cli`).

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: plugin tool hooks are part of the extension surface (`claim-opencode-w2-extension-stack`).
- Extensions: local or npm plugins and plugin hooks are separate from MCP and skills (`claim-opencode-w2-extension-stack`, `claim-opencode-w2-mcp`, `claim-opencode-w2-skills`).
- MCP: local and remote MCP are documented, with an unresolved docs/code implementation gap (`claim-opencode-w2-mcp`, `claim-opencode-w2-tools-code-doc-gap`).
- Skills: multi-scope on-demand skills are documented (`claim-opencode-w2-skills`).
- Hooks: command, message, permission, server, session, tool, TUI, and compaction plugin hooks are documented (`claim-opencode-w2-extension-stack`).
- APIs: OpenAPI/SDK server and ACP subprocess are separate (`claim-opencode-w2-surface-acp-api`, `claim-opencode-w2-acp`).

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: Build and Plan can invoke General, Explore, and Scout (`claim-opencode-w2-orchestration`).
- Parallelism: different session keys can run concurrently; isolated worktrees or security boundaries are not established (`claim-opencode-w2-orchestration`).

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: OpenCode says it does not sandbox the agent (`claim-opencode-w2-security`, `claim-opencode-w2-not-for`).
- Permissions: allow, ask, and deny are granular UX controls rather than a security boundary (`claim-opencode-w2-permissions`, `claim-opencode-w2-security`).
- Security: network server authentication is operator-managed; an unset password leaves the exposed server unsecured (`claim-opencode-w2-security`, `claim-opencode-w2-drawback`).
- Data path: local SQLite state and public share sync are distinct paths (`claim-opencode-w2-local-storage`, `claim-opencode-w2-data-path`).

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
- Interface and surface IDs:
  - Terminal: `surface-opencode-cli-tui`, `surface-opencode-cli-run` (`claim-opencode-w2-surface-cli`).
  - Web: `surface-opencode-web-local`, `surface-opencode-web-lan` (`claim-opencode-w2-surface-web`).
  - Direct remote clients: `surface-opencode-attach-tui`, `surface-opencode-desktop-remote-http` (`claim-opencode-w2-surface-attach`, `claim-opencode-w2-surface-desktop`).
  - Desktop and IDE: `surface-opencode-desktop-local`, `surface-opencode-desktop-wsl`, `surface-opencode-ide` (`claim-opencode-w2-surface-desktop`, `claim-opencode-w2-surface-ide`).
  - APIs: `surface-opencode-acp`, `surface-opencode-local-api` (`claim-opencode-w2-acp`, `claim-opencode-w2-surface-acp-api`).
  - CI: `surface-opencode-github-actions` (`claim-opencode-w2-surface-ci`).
  - Hosted transcript: `surface-opencode-share-page` (`claim-opencode-w2-surface-share`).
- Remote behavior: direct HTTP/LAN attachment to a running backend; no vendor relay was established (`claim-opencode-w2-surface-attach`, `claim-opencode-w2-surface-desktop`, `claim-opencode-w2-mobile-messaging-relay-unknown`).
- Mobile behavior: native mobile and mobile-web support remain unknown. LAN browser access is not treated as mobile support (`claim-opencode-w2-mobile-messaging-relay-unknown`, `claim-opencode-w2-surface-web`).
- Background behavior: a GitHub Actions runner route exists; arbitrary local background execution and a hosted interactive workspace remain unknown (`claim-opencode-w2-surface-ci`).

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: the runtime/provider/service split, Zen PAYG balance, Go subscription, and Enterprise per-seat quote are separate claims (`claim-opencode-w2-pricing`, `claim-opencode-w2-pricing-services`, `claim-opencode-w2-pricing-go`, `claim-opencode-w2-pricing-enterprise`).
- License: MIT (`claim-opencode-w2-license`).
- Maintenance: active v1.18.16 release (`claim-opencode-w2-status`).
- Lock-in: local source, providers, API, SDK, and ACP provide technical exit paths; hosted auth, share, Zen, Go, and provider services remain separate dependencies (`claim-opencode-w2-unique`, `claim-opencode-w2-pricing`).

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: no checked first-party statement links the archived `opencode-ai/opencode` repository, which moved to Crush, to current `anomalyco/opencode` (`claim-opencode-w2-lineage`).
- Relationship edges: no new outgoing OpenCode row. Existing baseline inbound Kilo, Conductor, and T3 tuples were not copied.

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements
sections.body:
- Comparison neighborhood IDs: `unknown`; no new Wave 2 neighborhood row was emitted.
- Substitutes: `unknown`
- Partial substitutes: `unknown`
- Same-lineage relatives: `unknown`
- Often-confused products: archived `opencode-ai/opencode` and current Anomaly OpenCode share a name but no lineage was asserted (`claim-opencode-w2-lineage`).
- Complements: `unknown`

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: open, provider-flexible client/server runtime with local models and broad extension points (`claim-opencode-w2-unique`).
- Meaningful drawbacks: no agent sandbox and operator-managed network security (`claim-opencode-w2-drawback`).
- Best fit: no new Wave 2 intended-user claim was emitted; `unknown` in this candidate rather than a recommendation.
- Not-for: users requiring the agent itself to enforce sandbox isolation (`claim-opencode-w2-not-for`).
